subject: fluid_mechanics
title: Characteristics Studies of Gear Oil Pump
aim: To study the performance characteristics of a gear pump and to determine its operating heads, discharge rate, input power, output power, and overall efficiency.
apparatus: Gear pump coupled with 2.0 HP motor (1440 rpm)
Sump tank and collecting tank (0.25 m × 0.25 m)
Vacuum gauge on suction side (mm Hg)
Gauge glass scale for oil level rise
theory:
The gear oil pump is a positive displacement machine consisting of two identical intermeshing spur wheels working with a fine clearance inside the casing. One gear is keyed to the driving shaft and the other revolves as the driven wheel. As the gears rotate, fluid (oil) is trapped between the tooth spaces and the casing wall, transported along the outer periphery from the suction side, and forced out into the delivery pipe under pressure.

Suction Head:
H_s = \frac{P_s \times 133.3}{\rho g} = \frac{P_s \times 133.3}{8770} = P_s \times 0.0152 \quad (\text{m of oil})

Delivery Head:
H_d = \frac{P_d \times 9.81 \times 10^4}{\rho g} = \frac{P_d \times 9.81 \times 10^4}{8770} = P_d \times 11.185 \quad (\text{m of oil})

Total Operating Head:
H_T = H_d + H_s + Z \quad (\text{m of oil}) \quad \text{where } Z = 0.15\text{ m}

Actual Volumetric Discharge Rate:
Q_{act} = \frac{A_{tank} \times rise}{t} = \frac{0.25 \times 0.25 \times 0.1}{t} = \frac{0.00625}{t} \quad (\text{m}^3/\text{s})

Electrical Input Power:
I_p = \frac{N \times 3600 \times 1000}{T \times 1200} = \frac{30000}{T} \quad (\text{Watts})

Pump Hydraulic Output Power:
O_p = \rho \cdot g \cdot H_T \cdot Q_{act} = 8770 \times H_T \times Q_{act} \quad (\text{Watts})

Overall Pump Efficiency:
\eta = \frac{O_p}{I_p} \times 100 \quad (\%)
procedure: Before starting the experiment, verify that the delivery regulating valve is completely open.
Switch on the electric motor to run the gear oil pump at rated speed (1440 rpm).
Adjust the delivery pressure regulating valve to establish the desired delivery gauge reading (Pd).
Record the suction vacuum gauge reading (Ps in mm Hg) and delivery pressure gauge reading (Pd in kgf/cm²).
Close the collecting tank drain valve and measure the time taken (t in sec) for a 10 cm (0.1 m) oil level rise.
Record the time taken (T in sec) for 10 revolutions of the energy meter disc using a stopwatch.
Repeat the observations for 5 different delivery pressure settings spanning the operating range.
Compute Hs, Hd, HT, Qact, Ip, Op, and overall pump efficiency η for each trial.

formulas.label: Suction Head (Hs)
formulas.derivation: Conversion of suction vacuum gauge reading in mm Hg to equivalent meters of oil column using specific weight of oil γ = 8770 N/m³:\n\nH_s = \\frac{P_s \\times 133.322}{8770} = P_s \\times 0.0152 \\text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates suction lift head in meters of oil.
formulas.practical_application: Quantifies suction vacuum lift required to draw viscous oil into the pump gears.

formulas.label: Delivery Head (Hd)
formulas.purpose: Calculates delivery discharge head in meters of oil.
formulas.practical_application: Measures effective delivery pressure head overcome by the meshing gears.

formulas.label: Total Head (HT)
formulas.derivation: Sum of delivery head, suction head, and gauge centerline datum difference Z = 0.15 m:\n\nH_T = H_d + H_s + 0.15 \\text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Determines total manometric head developed by the gear pump.
assumptions: Vertical distance between gauge centers = 0.15 m
formulas.practical_application: Basis for pump hydraulic power output and total dynamic head evaluation.

formulas.label: Actual Discharge Rate (Qact)
formulas.derivation: Volumetric flow rate from collecting tank dimensions (0.25 m × 0.25 m) and 10 cm level rise:\n\nQ_{act} = \\frac{0.00625}{t} \\text{ (m}^3\\text{/s)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates actual volumetric flow rate delivered by the gear pump.
assumptions: Uniform tank cross section of 0.25 m × 0.25 m
formulas.practical_application: Assesses positive displacement volumetric capacity of the gear pump.

formulas.label: Electrical Input Power (Ip)
formulas.derivation: Calculated from energy meter disc revolutions and energy meter constant 1200 rev/kWh:\n\nI_p = \\frac{10 \\times 3600 \\times 1000}{T \\times 1200} = \\frac{30000}{T} \\text{ (Watts)}
formulas.purpose: Measures total electric power supplied to the motor driving the pump.

variables.meaning: Time for 10 revs of energy meter disc

assumptions: Standard utility energy meter constant of 1200 rev/kWh
formulas.practical_application: Determines electrical energy consumption of the pump unit.

formulas.label: Pump Hydraulic Output Power (Op)
formulas.latex: O_p = \\rho g \\cdot H_T \\cdot Q_{act} = 8770 \\times H_T \\times Q_{act}
formulas.derivation: Hydraulic work done on the fluid per unit time:\n\nO_p = \\gamma \\cdot H_T \\cdot Q_{act} = 8770 \\times H_T \\times Q_{act} \\text{ (Watts)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates useful hydraulic work transferred to the pumped fluid.
formulas.practical_application: Measures useful energy delivered to the oil stream.

formulas.label: Overall Pump Efficiency (η)
formulas.derivation: Ratio of useful hydraulic power output to gross electrical power input:\n\n\\eta = \\frac{O_p}{I_p} \\times 100 \\text{ (\\%)}
formulas.purpose: Measures overall energy conversion efficiency of the gear oil pump set.
assumptions: Combined motor and gear pump mechanical-hydraulic set
formulas.practical_application: Identifies operating performance and maximum efficiency operating point.

precautions: Before starting the experiment, verify that the delivery regulating valve is completely open.
Ensure the oil sump tank contains clean lubricating oil without moisture or foreign particles.
Operate the delivery pressure regulating valve gently and monitor pressure gauge limits.
